subject: DPA and subprocessor notification window - redlines and signature
messages:
From: Sarah Coleman <sarah.coleman@acmehealth.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Acme DPA - subprocessor notification window and next steps

Hi Dev,

Thanks for the run-through on Friday. Attached is Acme Health's redline of the standard DPA (file: Acme_Counter_Redline_v2.pdf). Two items we want to make sure are captured before we execute:

- Notification window for new subprocessors: Acme's legal prefers a 60-day notice for additions to the subprocessor list, with details on purpose and data access.
- Objection process: we expect an escalation path with reasonable timelines for review and mitigation, and the ability to suspend transfer only after good-faith attempts to resolve.

Can you confirm Redwood's standard position on both? Also please point me to where you prefer to execute (DocuSign or AdobeSign) and whether you can accept our redline or propose compromise language.

We are aiming to close the DPA this month to align with procurement and our vendor onboarding.

Thanks,
Sarah Coleman
Senior Counsel, Acme Health
Sarah.Coleman@acmehealth.com

Attachment: Acme_Counter_Redline_v2.pdf

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sarah Coleman <sarah.coleman@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme DPA - subprocessor notification window and next steps

Hi Sarah,

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the redline. Looping in Marissa from legal and Karthik from product so we can align on the operational side. Laura from Sales Ops is cc'd to keep procurement timelines in view.

High level from Redwood:
- We typically publish a subprocessor list and provide a 30-day advance notice for routine additions. That gives customers time to review and raise objections.
- For objection process, our standard is a documented review period (30 days), during which we'll collaborate on mitigations; only after failure to agree would there be a narrowly scoped suspension right. We try to avoid broad suspensions that impact availability.
- For major changes that introduce core analytics or new data processing locations, we understand customers may need longer notice; we're open to discussing an exception in the DPA.

Marissa — can you review Acme's proposed 60-day and suggest compromise language? We can prepare a redline that keeps the standard 30-day window but allows a 45-60 day window for critical categories via an exception list.

On execution: DocuSign works best for us. Once we have an agreed redline I will send the envelope and confirm signers.

I attached our standard DPA redline for reference (file: DPA_Redline_AcmeHealth_v3.pdf).

Next steps I propose:
1) Legal to exchange concise bullets on the notification window and objection steps (Marissa and Sarah)
2) Agree on final text and counter-sign via DocuSign
3) Post-signature: we will publish the subprocessor list and commit to the agreed notification cadence

If that works I can act as program owner on delivery.

Best,
Dev Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.inference.com

Attachment: DPA_Redline_AcmeHealth_v3.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sarah Coleman <sarah.coleman@acmehealth.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme DPA - subprocessor notification window and next steps

Hi Sarah and team,

Thanks for the redline and context. I reviewed Acme's proposed 60-day notice. Our recommended middle path is:

- Routine subprocessors (infrastructure, standard managed services): 30 days notice.
- Critical subprocessors (analytics, data enrichment, or new geo locations): 45 days notice and the right for Acme to object; an exception list can be maintained and updated by mutual agreement.

Suggested contract language (summary):
- Redwood will publish a subprocessor list and provide notice of material additions. For routine additions, Redwood will notify Controller no less than 30 days prior to engagement. For additions that will process personal data in a materially different manner or new jurisdictions, Redwood will provide no less than 45 days notice. Controller may object within the notice period with a written statement of reasonable grounds. Parties will engage in good-faith efforts to resolve objections; suspension rights are limited and tied to specific processing activities.

Operational notes: we have an internal SOP for subprocessor onboarding and emergency escalations (internal doc link below). If Acme prefers a longer window for certain categories we can put those on an exception schedule.

Internal doc: https://redwoodinference.internal/sops/subprocessor-onboarding (internal access)

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com

From: Sarah Coleman <sarah.coleman@acmehealth.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme DPA - subprocessor notification window and next steps

Marissa, Dev,

Thanks for the clear compromise language. Acme is generally comfortable with the split 30/45 approach for routine vs critical subprocessors. A couple of follow-ups:

- For critical subprocessors we will request a 60-day window in cases where the subprocessor will be engaging in sensitive analytics on patient-derived data. We propose that the DPA reference an exception schedule where Acme can flag those categories.
- Objection process: we want a defined SLA for initial legal review (15 business days) before escalation to execs.

I've attached a short counter-redline with these points (file: Acme_Counter_Redline_v2.pdf). If Redwood accepts, please send the final DPA via DocuSign with the signatory names below.

Signers:
- Acme Health: Sarah Coleman, Senior Counsel (sign)
- Redwood: authorized signatory (please let us know who will sign)

If you can send the DocuSign envelope by end of day tomorrow we can route on our side for procurement review.

Thanks,
Sarah

Attachment: Acme_Counter_Redline_v2.pdf

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.inference.com>

Subject: Re: Acme DPA - subprocessor notification window and next steps

Great — glad we have a path forward. Per the thread above, Redwood accepts the 30/45 compromise and a narrowly scoped 60-day exception for sensitive analytics subprocessors on patient-derived data; we will capture the exception schedule as discussed. We also accept the 15-business-day review SLA for objections as a good-faith target.

I have prepared the final DPA incorporating the agreed language and started a DocuSign envelope for signatures. DocuSign envelope: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/12345ABCDEF

Requested signers: Redwood authorized signer (Legal Ops) and Sarah Coleman for Acme. Laura — can you confirm on our side who will be listed as the signer?

- After signature we will publish the current subprocessor list and commit to the notification cadence in the DPA.
- Dev to follow up on onboarding checklist and set up an operational kickoff with Karthik.
